scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Promotion of Piggery Entrepreneur
description:
The National Livestock Mission: Promotion of Piggery Entrepreneur is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the livelihoods of farmers and promote entrepreneurship in the livestock sector. 

The scheme was launched in 2014 as part of the National Livestock Mission which aims to promote sustainable development of the livestock sector in India. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to increase the production of pork and improve the quality of pig farming in the country. 

The mission aims to enhance the income of farmers involved in pig farming by providing them with the necessary resources and support. 

The scheme targets a 20 percent increase in pig production over a five-year period from its inception in 2014. 

It also aims to promote the establishment of pig breeding farms and improve the genetic quality of pigs in India. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for the establishment of pig farms, training programs for farmers, and access to quality breeding stock. 

Under this scheme, farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 1.5 lakh for establishing a piggery unit. 

The scheme also provides for the establishment of pig breeding units with a subsidy of 50 percent of the project cost. 

Farmers can receive a subsidy of up to INR 1 lakh for purchasing breeding pigs. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of training and capacity building for farmers. 

Training programs are conducted to educate farmers about modern pig farming techniques and best practices. 

The training includes topics such as feeding, breeding, health management, and disease control. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers must be at least 18 years old to apply for the scheme. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility. 

The income criteria for eligibility are set at a maximum annual income of INR 1 lakh for small farmers and INR 2 lakh for marginal farmers. 

Applicants must possess a minimum educational qualification of 8th grade to be eligible for the scheme. 

The application process involves several steps that must be followed to ensure successful enrollment in the program. 

Farmers must first visit the official website of the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying to obtain the application form. 

The application form can be downloaded and printed for completion. 

Farmers must provide personal details such as name, address, and contact information in the application form. 

They must also include details about the proposed piggery unit, including the number of pigs to be raised and the type of housing to be constructed. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card, proof of residence, and income certificate. 

Farmers must also submit a project report outlining the proposed piggery unit's operational plan and financial projections. 

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the local veterinary officer or the district animal husbandry department. 

The application will be reviewed by the concerned authorities, and if approved, financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs within 30 days of approval of the application. 

The scheme also includes provisions for regular monitoring and evaluation of the piggery units established under the program. 

Farmers are encouraged to maintain records of their operations to facilitate monitoring. 

The implementing authority for the scheme is the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The department responsible for overseeing the implementation at the state level is the Department of Animal Husbandry. 

Farmers can contact their local animal husbandry department for assistance with the application process. 

The scheme has a significant impact on rural livelihoods by providing an alternative source of income for farmers. 

It also contributes to food security by increasing the availability of pork in the market. 

The promotion of pig farming is particularly beneficial in northeastern states where pig farming is a traditional practice. 

The scheme aims to empower women by encouraging their participation in pig farming activities. 

Women farmers are provided with additional training and support to enhance their skills in pig farming. 

The government has also initiated awareness campaigns to promote the nutritional benefits of pork. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of cooperatives among pig farmers to enhance collective bargaining power. 

Financial literacy programs are also conducted to help farmers manage their finances effectively. 

The National Livestock Mission aims to create a sustainable ecosystem for livestock farming in India. 

The promotion of pig farming is aligned with the government's broader goals of enhancing agricultural productivity and rural development. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall growth of the livestock sector in India. 

The government has set a target of increasing the overall livestock production by 25 percent by 2025. 

The promotion of piggery entrepreneurship is a crucial component of this target. 

The scheme is part of a larger strategy to promote animal husbandry as a viable livelihood option for rural communities. 

The government is committed to providing ongoing support and resources to farmers involved in pig farming. 

The National Livestock Mission: Promotion of Piggery Entrepreneur is a vital initiative that aims to transform the livelihoods of farmers across India. 

It provides a comprehensive framework for promoting pig farming as a sustainable and profitable venture. 

The scheme is designed to empower farmers with the knowledge and resources needed to succeed in pig farming. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme and make necessary adjustments to enhance its effectiveness. 

The promotion of pig farming is expected to play a significant role in achieving the goals of the National Livestock Mission. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of farmers and promoting rural development in India. 

Farmers interested in the scheme are encouraged to take advantage of the resources and support available to them. 

The National Livestock Mission: Promotion of Piggery Entrepreneur is a promising opportunity for farmers to enhance their income and contribute to the growth of the livestock sector.
